thread:
mike_acme: Hey team — my console shows me as Org Admin (top-right badge) but when I try to create a new API key under project `payments` I get a 403. This started right after we re-bound our SSO connector (Okta) yesterday. Repro steps: 
1) Login via SSO -> see Org Admin badge
2) Go to project payments -> Settings -> API keys -> Create new key
3) Click Create -> UI modal fails with toast: `Forbidden (403)`
I can create keys using our service account outside the console (curl) so seems UI-specific. Any ideas?

jen_supp: Thanks @mike_acme — sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the exact error payload from the devtools network tab (response body) and a timestamp when you saw it? Also, did you re-auth after the SSO binding change? :thinking_face:

mike_acme: attaching a snippet from the network tab (sanitized): ```json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "insufficient_scope: required scopes [org.write, project.keys.create], token has [org.read]",
  "code": 403
}
```
I re-logged in once, but several teammates did a full browser restart. Happened at 2024-05-03T14:12:08Z (UTC).

matt_id: @jen_supp looping in identity team. That error text strongly implies the session token the console is using has a reduced scope (org.read only). Two likely causes: 1) SSO claim mapping changed so groups -> role mapping now issues a narrower scope, or 2) the console is still using a stale delegated token (token aliasing) after the connector rebind. Can you try a hard re-auth (incognito, full logout + clear cookies) and repro? Also share the `x-request-id` from the failing request if available.

mike_acme: tried incognito and full logout, still 403. x-request-id: "req_0a1b2c3d4e". For what it's worth, our org-level role in IdP is still "redwood-org-admin" and group membership shows in SCIM responses.

alice_sre: interesting note — I reproduced a similar symptom in staging when we changed the SSO claim name from `roles` -> `membership`. UI sessions kept old scopes until refresh token rotation. Workaround was to force the console to fetch a fresh session token (logout + revoke sessions from admin page) or generate a service account key. If service account key works for you (it did for @mike_acme earlier) we can use that to create keys while we debug.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: finished deploy 2024-05-03T13:50:00Z to identity-service (v3.4.7) — included fixes for claim-normalization.

matt_id: infra-bot noted a deploy recently; it's possible some nodes are on older claim-normalization code and some on newer, causing mixed-token behavior. @jen_supp please collect a trace for `req_0a1b2c3d4e` (auth service logs + identity-service logs) and escalate to eng-identity. Also confirm whether the failing request shows `Authorization: Bearer <session-token>` vs `x-api-key:` in the request — UI should be sending a session bearer with scopes.

jen_supp: got the trace request in. @mike_acme can you confirm whether any of your org admins still see the old behavior or is it just you? If it's org-wide we escalate to Priority 2. If it's just you we may look at session caching.

mike_acme: three other admins (elaine, jorge, and me) all fail. Elaine can create keys via curl using her service account but not via console.

matt_id: ok org-wide — bumping to eng-identity. Preliminary triage: probable root cause = claim name change in SSO mapping + gradual deploy left some auth frontends accepting older claim set and returning shorter scopes. Fix path: 1) run a one-time resync of session cache on identity frontends (force re-eval of role->scope), 2) invalidate stale console sessions (we can push a session-logout event for org admins), 3) backfill any tokens that were minted with wrong scopes if necessary. ETA after triage: ~2-4 hours.

jen_supp: I've opened INT-4829 for identity with the trace + request IDs and put a hold on customer operations. For now workaround steps for you: 
- Use a service account key to create the API key (what you said worked).
- Alternatively, have an Org Admin go to Admin > Sessions and Revoke sessions for affected users, then re-login.

mike_acme: revoke sessions worked for 1 admin (elaine) after she re-logged in — console can now create keys for her. Still failing for me and jorge. We'll do revoke/relogin for remaining folks and report back. Appreciate the quick triage. :rocket:

alice_sre: logging note for the incident: check for `scope_evaluation` entries in auth logs where `accepted_scopes` != `expected_scopes` for org admins between 2024-05-03T13:30 and 2024-05-03T14:30Z. That will show which frontends returned the older claim mapping.

jen_supp: thanks @alice_sre and @matt_id — I'll keep @mike_acme updated here and mark the thread as escalated. If anything changes please ping me. :thumbsup:

mike_acme: confirmed revoke+relogin fixed it for all admins, creating API key now succeeds. Thanks everyone.

jen_supp: closing loop — identity team patched a cache invalidation edge-case in v3.4.8 and completed a coordinated session purge. I'll follow up with the incident blameless postmortem link when available.
